_about: GENERATED from RFI canon by tools/convert-5e.mjs (rubric v1.11.0) — do not hand-edit; put fixes in content/overrides/secrets.json. The Courtly Intrigue secrets as dnd5e feats (the secret engine block carried verbatim).

items.name: A Name in the Wendigo's Book

description.value:
A Name in the Wendigo's Book. You happen to know whose reservation is coming up. You happen to mention it, within earshot, with a sad little smile. There was something a bit OFF about how fast they left.

Play: Deal 3 Influence damage to your opponent outside an exchange.

items.name: A Question Left on the Table

description.value:
A Question Left on the Table. No accusation. Just a question, asked loudly enough, that nobody present can answer without naming someone.

Play: +2 Suspicion — the court destabilizes (defection favors the Influence leader).

A Recess, Called by Nobody. Somebody rings a bell that is not on the agenda, and the whole court stops to listen to a train leave. Nobody loses anything in the next exchange — Influence stands where it was; scandal, Suspicion and marks still happen.

Play: the next exchange deals no Influence damage to either side.

Audit Notice. Every purse at the table is frozen pending review. No marks may be spent by either side next exchange.

Play: no marks may be spent by either side next exchange.
Blood Oath. A binding promise in red. Play: +2 Favor with a chosen courtier toward your side.

Buried Betrothal. A marriage promised before the Shattering, never formally dissolved. Wave it gently and watch a cold courtier suddenly find you fascinating.

Play: +2 Favor with a courtier of your choice toward your side.
Burned Ledger. The evidence is ash. Play: −2 Suspicion.

Cabinet Whisper. A choice morsel of intel from a sympathetic minister, delivered just before the moment of need.

Play: queue +2 to your next Parley roll.

Compromising Letter. A private correspondence — leaked at exactly the wrong moment for someone, exactly the right moment for you.

Play: deal 2 Influence damage to your opponent outside an exchange.

Counterfeit Truth, Notarized. A notary's seal on a thing nobody said. Your next stolen receipt plays as earned — no Suspicion, and the one you took it from never learns who carried it.

Play: your next stolen receipt plays as earned.
Crown Confidant. The sovereign's own ear. Play: queue +3 to your next Parley roll.

Forged Writ of Passage. The seal is real. The signature is real-adjacent. By the time anyone checks, you were demonstrably somewhere else, being charming.

Play: −2 Suspicion.

Itemized Receipts. Not a metaphor. Actual receipts. Itemized. Someone bought something they should not have, and kept the little slip of paper like an idiot.

Play: Deal 2 Influence damage to your opponent outside an exchange.

Marked Cards at the Salon. The game was rigged before you sat down. You rigged it. Sit down.

Play: +3 to your next Parley roll.

Misfiled Confession. Your sin is on record. The record is in a box. The box is, tragically, in the wrong archive, possibly on fire.

Play: Clear your own Scandal flag (if any).

Pre-Fall Blackmail Reel. Grainy footage from a world that ended. The haircut alone is ruinous. The rest is worse.

Play: Deal 2 Influence damage to your opponent outside an exchange.
Quiet Endorsement. A nod from the right box. Play: +1 Favor with a chosen courtier toward your side.

items.name: Round of Drinks on the House

description.value:
Round of Drinks on the House. Somebody is paying and it is you. Every courtier at the table warms to your side by one.

Play: +1 Favor with every courtier, your side.

Royal Pardon. A signed favor from a higher patron, granted in advance of a rumor's bloom.

Play: clear your own Scandal flag (if any).
Sealed Indictment. Charges nobody can quash. Play: deal 3 Influence damage outside an exchange.

Sealed Pardon, Pre-Signed. A blank pardon with a real signature, sold to you by someone who will deny it to their grave. Fill in your own name. Move along.

Play: Clear your own Scandal flag (if any).

Signed by Nobody. A contract of impossible provenance: terms nobody remembers setting, in language a shade older than the paper it's printed on, ending in a notarized, sealed, entirely blank signature block — and binding anyway. It does not explain anything. It unsettles everyone.

Play: queue −2 to your opponent's next Parley roll and +2 Suspicion — the court cannot stop wondering whose pen it was.

Sovereign Writ. A writ with a seal older than the court. Produce it and the next exchange is simply yours — the dice are read, and the record says you won by at least three.

Play: you win the next exchange outright.
Stacked Deck. You stacked it, they cut it, and it did not matter. Play: force your opponent to reroll their next exchange.

The Agenda, Amended in Pencil. The word at the top of the page is crossed out and another written above it in a hand everyone recognises. Change what this Parley is for — Persuade, Deceive, or Stay unnoticed.

Play: rewrite the stake — change what this Parley is for.

The Auditor's Ledger. A column of numbers that do not add up the way someone swore they did. Names attached. Dates attached. Interest, compounding.

Play: Deal 3 Influence damage to your opponent outside an exchange.

The Long Memory of Mal. "Oh, THAT? No no, I didn't log that. Must've been a cosmic-ray bit-flip. Happens. You're welcome. We never spoke." — the narrator, doing you a solid.

Play: −2 Suspicion.

The Misprinted Invitation. Their seat card reads a name that is not theirs, at a table that was not set for them. They will spend the whole exchange recovering.

Play: queue −2 to your opponent's next Parley roll.

The Pickpocket's Apology. A note in the opponent's pocket where a secret used to be: SORRY. They discard a stolen receipt at random.

Play: your opponent discards a random stolen receipt.

The Price List. Filed under WEATHER: who in this court wants what, and what it costs. Every courtier's favor toward both sides, and the court bonus each side carries, whispered to you alone.

Play: every courtier's favor, both sides, whispered to you.

The Quartermaster's Debt. You covered a shortfall once, quietly, and never mentioned it. Now you mention it. Just once. Just enough.

Play: +1 Favor with a courtier of your choice toward your side.

The Room Remembers Differently. A page comes out of the minutes so cleanly that everyone agrees it was never there. Influence, Suspicion, scandal and the round go back to before the last exchange; the marks spent in it stay spent.

Play: strike the last exchange from the record.

The Sommelier Knows. Who drank what, with whom, and how much courage it took them. Vintages are memory. The sommelier has an excellent memory.

Play: +2 to your next Parley roll.

The Understudy's Grudge. Every favored courtier stands on someone who wanted that spot. That someone remembers. That someone has a price, and it is mostly spite.

Play: Flip a courtier: −1 Favor toward your opponent, +1 toward you.

The Wrong Twin. You introduce a small, load-bearing uncertainty about who, exactly, your opponent has been dealing with all evening.

Play: Your opponent must reroll their next exchange.
Turned Courtier. Their friend is your friend now. Play: flip a courtier — −1 to the opponent, +1 to you.

Two Tongues, One Table. Tell each of them what the other said. You don't even have to lie much. Mostly you just have to seat them adjacent.

Play: Two courtiers each lose 1 Favor toward your opponent.
Wedge of Doubt. Sow distrust in the gallery. Play: −1 Favor with two courtiers toward your opponent.

Whisper from the Scullery. The people who carry the trays hear everything and are paid to forget none of it — only to wait to be asked nicely.

Play: +2 to your next Parley roll.
